Interpretation boundary

Analytical reading

What this view can—and cannot—support

Can support

Describing how reported events, vessel categories and recorded outcomes are distributed within the published dataset.

Use caution

Comparing category counts where reporting practices, operating environments and fleet exposure differ.

Cannot support

Causal claims or true accident-rate rankings without a denominator and an appropriate research design.

Association, not causation

Severity & human consequences

This view moves beyond occurrence counts by retaining vessel- and person-level records. Results remain conditional on a reported occurrence and are not exposure-adjusted risk estimates.

MODEL SAMPLE—reported occurrences
SERIOUS OUTCOMES—serious / very serious
DISCRIMINATION—in-sample ROC AUC

Reading the model: an odds ratio above 1 indicates higher adjusted odds of a serious classification among reported occurrences. Confidence intervals crossing 1 are not statistically distinguishable from no association at the 95% level.

Decision boundary

The model asks which characteristics are associated with severity after an occurrence has entered the MAIB dataset. Without fleet size, voyages, distance travelled or operating hours, it cannot identify which vessel group has the highest accident risk.
